title: Point transport realizes the compatible finite coefficient transports
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, $\ell\ne p$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $\mathcal O_E$, $\varpi$, $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius $\gamma$, and let $N\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ be derived-complete integral constructible [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], with $N_n=N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$. Let $\mathcal R(N)$ be its coherent reduction tower from [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Use $\Gamma(s,-)=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the completed pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the point transports $\iota_N,\iota_{N_n}$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. The finite maps $\iota_{N_n}:\Gamma(s,N_n)\to\Gamma(s,Lg_s^*N_n)$ are evaluations of a morphism of the quotient-induced towers, with transitions obtained before passage to the derived categories of individual levels. Under the canonical completeness identifications
$$\Gamma(s,N)\simeq R\varprojlim_n\Gamma(s,N_n),\qquad
\Gamma(s,Lg_s^*N)\simeq R\varprojlim_n\Gamma(s,Lg_s^*N_n),$$
the realization of this tower morphism is $\iota_N$. In particular this is the integral map defined by part (b) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], rather than an arbitrary map having the same individual reductions. The identifications and this assertion are natural in $N$.

source.place: clause *(3)*: the integral point transport is the derived limit of the levelwise maps, via its specified cone map

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $q:P\to N$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Apply [lem-trf-point-transport-strict-quotient] to its simultaneous quotients. It supplies a strict map $u:D_\bullet\to B_\bullet$, with $D_n=\Gamma(s,P_n)$ and $B_n=\Gamma(s,\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n)$, whose evaluations are $\iota_{N_n}$. It also supplies the strict augmentation equality $\Gamma(s,\theta_n)\sigma_P=u_n\Gamma(s,r_n)$ needed below, and natural descent of the tower map. Thus compatibility is established before passage to individual derived levels.

source.place: clause (3), assembly of clause (3), simultaneous quotient transport: original realization proof steps 1-2 and chain/tower naturality in step 6

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-point-sections-completion-cone] to the same $P$. Its specified sectionwise cone comparison realizes $u$ by $H(u)$, diagonal on the two products. Its canonical isomorphisms $\alpha_N:\Gamma(s,N)\simeq H(D_\bullet)$ and $\beta_N:\Gamma(s,Lg_s^*N)\simeq H(B_\bullet)$ identify these cones with the asserted derived limits. Here $\alpha_N\Gamma(s,q)$ is the map $a_P:z\mapsto(0,(\Gamma(s,r_n)z)_n)$, and $\beta_N$ is identity on both sectionwise product components of the defining completed-pullback cone. These comparisons are natural in derived inputs and independent of the representative.

source.place: clause (3), assembly of clause (3), sectionwise shifted cone and canonical completion identifications: original realization proof steps 3-4 and comparison descent in step 6

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-point-transport-cone-comparison-descent] with the strict augmentation equality from step 1. It gives $b_q\iota_N\Gamma(s,q)=H(u)a_P$, and $b_q=\beta_N$: both are induced by $c_C$ on the defining completed-pullback cone of the same $P$ (step 2). Step 2 identifies $a_P=\alpha_N\Gamma(s,q)$; the cited cone/descent lemma makes $\Gamma(s,q)$ invertible. Cancel it to obtain $\beta_N\iota_N=H(u)\alpha_N$. The lemma uses the specified integral comparison (b), including its zero shifted-product component, so this proves equality of the actual integral map with the realization. Its roof descent, combined with the natural tower map of step 1 and natural comparisons of step 2, gives all assertions naturally for arbitrary derived morphisms of $N$.

source.place: clause (3), assembly of clause (3), actual comparison (b) on both cone components: original realization proof step 5 and derived-roof descent in step 6
